title: Name the most specific class
intro: Identity ⊂ Scalar ⊂ Diagonal ⊂ Square. Every card below is square — sort each into the tightest class that fits, not the loosest.

buckets.label: Identity
buckets.hint: kI with k = 1 — passes through untouched

cards.text: An inertia tensor after rotating the body to its principal axes
A MIMO channel matrix with perfect antenna isolation and unequal path losses
A balanced four-channel attenuator dropping every channel by the same 3 dB
The transform a vertex pipeline resets to before stacking model, view and projection
The matrix B for which AB = BA = A holds for every square A of that order
An inertia tensor with non-zero products of inertia Iₓᵧ and I_yz
A rotation matrix for 45° about the z-axis

debrief: Every card is diagonal-or-better in some loose sense only if you stop reading early — which is the habit this session is built to break. The three levels carry three different physical claims: **diagonal** means the axes are decoupled (a principal-axis inertia tensor is the whole reason pure roll torque produces pure roll acceleration); **scalar** means every axis gets the *same* treatment (a balanced attenuator, geometric similarity); **identity** means nothing happened at all. The two 'square, not diagonal' cards are the instructive ones. A tensor with non-zero products of inertia is a body whose axes fight each other — roll input bleeds into yaw — and the engineering move is to rotate until those terms vanish. And the 45° rotation is the reminder that *structure is not the same as niceness*: a rotation matrix is orthogonal, beautifully behaved, trivially invertible by transpose — and thoroughly non-diagonal, because rotating is exactly the act of mixing axes.
